newsitem.title: USA: U.S. praises Spain in diplomatic row with Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. praises Spain in diplomatic row with Cuba.

text.p: The United States praised Spain on Wednesday for criticising human rights practices in Cuba, a policy which has brought Madrid into a sharp diplomatic conflict with Havana.

"We're obviously very pleased that a European leader is now standing up to defend human rights and democracy in Cuba," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said of Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar.

Months of rising tension between Cuba and Spain's young conservative government boiled over on Tuesday when Havana accused Madrid of meddling in its affairs and withdrew the approval it had already given for a new Spanish ambassador.
After 13 years of Socialist rule, Spain has now taken a tougher line against Cuban President Fidel Castro and is nudging its European Union partners to press for democracy in Communist-ruled Cuba.

Burns told a news briefing the Cuban diplomatic action against Spain was not unexpected. "It's not surprising to us that this authoritarian leader -- the last in our hemisphere -- is acting in this irrational way," he said.

"Castro is not a reliable person in dealing with other countries. And it's probably one of the hallmarks of an authoritarian regime like Cuba's that when they have problems internally, they tend to lash out and blame people outside," he said.
Burns said Castro had been blaming the United States for the past 30 years for his problems "and maybe Spain is being included in that group."
For months the United States has been denouncing what it portrays as the spineless attitude of most European countries towards Cuba in opposing ever-tougher U.S. sanctions on Havana.
The European Union is seeking to retaliate against the U.S. law, passed earlier this year, which penalises foreign companies that utilize property seized by the Cuban government from U.S. citizens.
